question.worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{6}^{\infty }\frac{12}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{6}^{a}\frac{12}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{6}^{a}{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =12{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[(-{x}^{-1})]}_{6}^{a} \\  & =-12\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{x}]}_{6}^{a} \\  & =-12\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{a}-\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =-12(0-\frac{1}{6}) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
